*   **Vegan:** Means the product doesn't contain any animal-derived ingredients (like honey, beeswax, lanolin, etc.). Cruelty-free and vegan aren't the same – a product can be cruelty-free but not vegan, and vice versa.

**Common Labels & Certifications:**

*   **Leaping Bunny:** This is a widely recognized and stringent certification. *   **PETA's Beauty Without Bunnies:** PETA (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals) also has its own certification. It's similar to Leaping Bunny, but some consider it less rigorous in its supply chain verification. [https://www.peta.org/features/beauty-without-bunnies/](https://www.peta.org/features/beauty-without-bunnies/)

*   **"Cruelty-Free" Claim (without a logo):** Be cautious with this one. Any company can *claim* to be cruelty-free without independent verification. Look for further information on their website about their testing policies.

*   **"Not Tested on Animals" vs. "Cruelty-Free":** "Not tested on animals" simply means the final product wasn't tested on animals. "Cruelty-free" ideally encompasses the entire production process, including ingredients and suppliers.

**Resources for More Information:**

*   **Cruelty-Free Kitty:** [https://www.crueltyfreekitty.com/](https://www.crueltyfreekitty.com/)
*   **Logical Harmony:** [https://logicalharmony.net/](https://logicalharmony.net/)
